subject: Private deployment delivery playbook: next steps for VPC peering & on‑prem connector
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-08-01T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Private deployment delivery playbook: next steps for VPC peering & on‑prem connector

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for the productive kickoff today. As discussed, I put together a concise delivery playbook so both teams have the same expectations for the private deployment (VPC peering, private endpoints, and on‑prem connector). Attached is a checklist and a vpc template to accelerate networking work.

High-level asks for your infra team before the technical deep dive: 
- Confirm the CIDR blocks you’ll reserve for the peered VPC and any overlapping ranges to avoid (we recommend /16 or /20 depending on scale).
- Share a primary contact for DirectConnect/ExpressRoute coordination and timing windows for circuit provisioning.
- Provide a short list of allowed egress IPs if you plan to constrain outbound egress for the appliance.

Proposed timeline (we can adjust):
- Week 0 (this week): exchange network inventory + sign off on CIDRs and peering window
- Week 1: runbook review and test credentials (canary keys)
- Week 2: peering and endpoint validation in staging
- Week 3: on‑prem connector install & smoke tests

Can we schedule a 45‑minute technical runthrough on Wednesday 8/4 at 11:00 PT? Marcus will lead the runbook walk.

Thanks — looking forward to making this low‑friction.

— Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Senior Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com
+1 415‑555‑0184

Thanks Lauren — this is great and very actionable. Quick answers from our side: 
- CIDR: we'll allocate 10.40.0.0/16 for the peered VPC. No current overlaps with our on‑prem ranges, but I'll attach our network inventory to the infra alias.
- DirectConnect: primary contact is infra@aperturebio.com. We have a ticket with our colo provider opening on 8/6; estimated 2–3 week lead time depending on circuit type.
- Egress policy: we'll restrict outbound to a small NAT pool (10.40.0.100–10.40.0.140) while the connector is in canary.

Weds 8/4 11:00 PT works for us. Marcus — can you confirm who from your end should join for the peering ACL discussion?

Subject: Re: Private deployment delivery playbook: next steps for VPC peering & on‑prem connector

Alex / team —
Appreciate the CIDR confirmation. A few technical notes I'll cover on the call but wanted to preface in writing: 
1) BGP + routing: we prefer establishing BGP session with MD5 auth for resilience. Please confirm ASN you'd like us to use (we can use 64512 by default).
2) ACLs: attach a minimal example below — allow 443/TCP to our private endpoint IPs and ephemeral TCP ranges for management when needed. We'll share a security justification doc.
3) KMS: if you'd like the Redwood on‑prem connector to encrypt cached inference artifacts using your KMS, we'll need a role/service principal and an IAM policy granting Encrypt/Decrypt for the connector service account.

Minimal ACL example (for discussion):
- Allow: ApertureBio CIDR 10.40.0.0/16 -> Redwood peering subnets on 443/TCP
- Allow: Management CIDR X.X.X.X/32 (your jump host) -> connector management port 8200/TCP

I attached the network diagram and an editable vpc-peering-template.yaml for your infra to iterate.

See you 8/4 — Marcus (will own the runbook section).
Marcus Lin
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Private deployment delivery playbook: next steps for VPC peering & on‑prem connector

Alex — thanks for the questions. Answers below and next actions: 

1) Private endpoints:
- Staging FQDNs (shortlived): staging-pvt-01.ap-n.Redwood.local -> 10.200.5.12
- Prod FQDNs (final): pvt-api.redwoodinference.internal -> 10.210.8.20
(These IPs are allocated to the peered subnets; final IPs will be confirmed at provisioning time.)

2) Installer / OS requirements:
- Supported: RHEL 8+, CentOS Stream 8+, Ubuntu 20.04+.
- Kernel modules: none required beyond standard networking; we ship a lightweight systemd service. Provide sudo-capable account for install.

3) Smoke tests: we will run three quick flows — connectivity, authentication (signed JWT exchange), and a small inference quality check using a 50‑record prompt set. Please provide a test S3 bucket or temporary signed URL for the 50 record sample.

Next actions (owners & ETA):
- Alex / Aperture infra: confirm final CIDR lock and share test bucket by 2027‑08‑11 (owner: infra@aperturebio.com).
- Marcus / Redwood: push a canary installer and onboarding runbook draft to the shared Drive folder by 2027‑08‑10.
- Karthik / Redwood: prepare KMS role template and IAM example by 2027‑08‑12.
- Lauren / Redwood: coordinate a go/no‑go sync on 2027‑08‑13 for staging validation.

If that timeline looks good we’ll schedule the go/no‑go. Thanks — excited to get ApertureBio into a private environment.

— Lauren
